name: wealthy
description: Recognition that you have a valued asset that many others may not have.
perceptions: I have something that others would like to have.

guidance.description: People with 'enough' money often don't feel wealthy. If you have a solid net worth, this article is worth considering.
Feeling 'wealthy' in something besides money may lead to satisfaction or gratitude. This article has suggestions for 'Choosing Gratitude Over Anxiety'.

variations.name: wealthy in a scarce resource
variations.description: A sense that you have more of a valued physical asset than many others.
perceptions: I have something that others would like to have.

commentaries.quote: 'Scarce' means that since you have that item, no one else can.

variations.name: wealthy in a non-scarce resource
variations.description: A sense that you have more of a valued social or mental asset than many others.
perceptions: I have something that others would like to have.
Pretty much everyone could have this if they spent the time and effort.

commentaries.quote: 'Non-scarce' means that you having some doesn't keep it from others.

variations.name: wealth anxiety
variations.description: A sense that you have more of a valued social or mental asset than many others, along with anxiety about someone being jealous or trying to take it from you.
perceptions: I have something that others would like to have.
Someone might try to take it from me or they might be jealous of it.

guidance.description: Instant fortune can be a huge burden, creating severe financial and emotional challenges. Getting to grips with suddenly having an enormous amount of money may seem like a good problem to have, but it can be the catalyst for a spectrum of psychological health issues.

examples: He has a great fossil collection, but won't show it to anyone.

commentaries.quote: People need all different kinds of stuff. Our brain keeps track of who has how much of each kind, and this bookkeeping causes all sorts of emotions: from admiration and inspiration to envy and anger.
We are all wealthy in something, and could become even more rich in friends, skill, or health.
Health is the greatest gift, contentment the greatest wealth, faithfulness the best relationship.
Lost wealth may be replaced by industry, lost knowledge by study, lost health by temperance or medicine, but lost time is gone forever.
It is not the creation of wealth that is wrong, but the love of money for its own sake.
